answer:
I've left early-warning signals out because your notes mark them as already reviewed. A first look shows four things worth checking next. Zimmer Biomet has 3,112 uncemented hip reports for 2022–2024, rising from 701 in 2022 to 1,329 in 2024 (+89.6%).

**Options, based on the data:**

1. **Find out why reports grew.** Break the 2022→2024 rise down by failure mode and quarter. That shows whether one mode (e.g. instability) is driving it or the growth is spread evenly. Reports for the latest months are still coming in, so 2024 may rise further.
2. **Look closer at instability, the largest failure mode.** It accounts for 662 reports (21.3%). One recall, [Z-1294-2023], removed CoCr Femoral Head XS compatibility with Epsilon Durasul constrained liners because their range of motion was below the recommended level. We could search report text for that combination to see whether instability reports mention it.
3. **Compare surgery problems with the recalls for mislabeled sizes.** 432 reports (13.9%) are problems during surgery, a category that includes "wrong size." Two recalls involved a package labeled with a different size than the part inside: [Z-1284-2023] (liner labeled 40 mm, actually 38 mm) and [Z-0418-2026] (Vivacit-E Dual Mobility Bearing, sizes swapped). Report text could show whether sizing complaints cluster around these.
4. **Compare against competitors.** Zimmer Biomet has 19.2% of all uncemented hip reports, behind DePuy Synthes (60.6%) and ahead of Stryker (10.3%). Comparing failure-mode shares across companies would show whether Zimmer Biomet's mix (e.g. 14.0% wear, 8.9% implant fracture) stands out. Shares don't depend on company size the way raw counts do.

**Caveats:**
- Report counts are not failure rates, because there's no figure for how many devices are in use.
- Failure modes are mapped from FDA problem terms and agree with reference labels about 70% of the time.
- The 17.4% "other/unknown" group limits how precise any breakdown can be.

Which would you like to start with? If you want, I can also save any of these to the investigation memory as an open question.
